_doc: Parse-time vessel rules as DATA — the MUSTs the parse prompt states about WHERE THE SAMPLE SITS, checked on every parse. One file, two readers: core/validate.py (the parse gate and the live API) and web/frontend/scripts/lib/vesselRules.mjs (schema-audit). Both walk the SAMPLE steps (a `prepare` is on the side and is skipped), tracking the sample's current vessel. `when` selects steps: action (one or a list), first_sample_step, or enters (the step names this vessel while the sample is elsewhere). `require` must then hold: container (an exact vessel, or "named" = any known vessel) or action. Only rules no correct parse breaks belong here. `evidence.kind` is honest: "real" if a real parse has broken it, "hand-edited-only" if it has only gone red on a hand-edited fixture — a rule that has never fired on real data may be encoding a belief rather than a constraint.
